project_overview: This Vue.js application appears to be a complex educational platform managing exam submissions, results, and user interactions. The core functionality revolves around several Vue components, including examination forms, result displays, and user dashboards. The application’s architecture utilizes Vue Router for navigation and likely leverages Vuex for state management (though not explicitly defined).  The dependency graph reveals a significant reliance on several core components for routing and displaying information.

layers.description: Contains application logic and data processing.

macro_trends.title: High-Level View Routing Domination
macro_trends.description: Multiple Vue components (ApplicationServices, ExamFormSubmission, ResultPage, etc.) are heavily reliant on Router push navigation. This creates a single point of failure and makes updates to the routing structure complex and prone to cascading errors.  The centralized routing contributes to a fragile architecture.

macro_trends.title: Component Dependency Concentration
macro_trends.description: Several components (ExamFormSubmission, ResultPage, SelectedApplicationService) are heavily connected, potentially creating a 'God Component' if their responsibilities expand significantly. This can lead to increased complexity and maintenance challenges.  The core components need review.

key_workflows.name: Exam Submission & Result Processing
key_workflows.description: This workflow involves the user submitting an exam form (ExamFormSubmission), data processing, and the display of results (ResultPage). The flow connects through several Vue components, each handling a specific step of the process. This is the most critical workflow and heavily relies on the routing described above.
